body:
VERIFIED against the code 2026-08-21. Surfaced by /security-review on PR #1781, which
correctly scoped it OUT as pre-existing. It is out of scope for that diff and squarely
in scope for the product: it defeats an invariant the code explicitly claims.

## The claimed invariant

cps/progress_syncing/protocols/koreader_annotations.py:64-67, verbatim:

    # Sources a push may delete from. A device may only delete rows of the source it
    # actually owns, so a KOReader sync can never touch a Kobo-native or web-reader
    # highlight.
    _DELETABLE_SOURCES = {"koreader"}

and _apply_deletes selects stale rows with `ub.Annotation.source == source`.

So the deletion boundary is entirely `Annotation.source`.

## The hole

`cps/services/annotation_portable.py:150-151`, on the EXISTING-row branch:

    elif payload.get("source") in _VALID_SOURCES:
        row.source = payload.get("source")

A push may set an existing row's `source` to any valid value. Nothing requires the new
value to match the row's current source, and nothing requires the pusher to own it.

## The two-step consequence

1. A KOReader push names an existing `kobo` or `webreader` annotation by its
   annotation_id and declares `source: "koreader"`. The row's source flips.
2. A subsequent push omits that annotation_id, so `_apply_deletes` sees it as stale --
   and it now matches `source == 'koreader'`, so it is deleted.

Net: a KOReader sync CAN delete a Kobo-native or web-reader highlight, which is exactly
what the comment says can never happen. The annotation_ids are not secret from the
client -- KOReader syncs them down, so it knows them.

## Why this is the same class as tonight's sweep

It is the F-947bb8 / #1657-comment pattern again at the authority layer: a PROSE
INVARIANT that the code does not enforce. The comment is what makes the missing check
invisible -- a reader checking "can KOReader delete a Kobo highlight?" reads the comment,
finds an explicit no, and stops.

## Scope, honestly

- OBSERVED: the code path, the assignment, and the delete predicate, by reading them.
- OBSERVED, EXECUTED 2026-08-21. I drove the two-push sequence through the REAL Flask
  route (`PUT /kosync/syncs/annotations`) using the repo's own `wire` fixture, against a
  row seeded with `source="kobo"`:

      STEP1 status=200  row.source='koreader'      <- the flip
      STEP2 status=200  deleted=1
      SURVIVING: set()                             <- the Kobo highlight is GONE

  Server logs for the same run:
      KOReader annotation push: ... created=0 updated=1 deleted=0   (the flip)
      annotation_sync: soft-delete annotation_id=kobo-1 (hidden=True)
      KOReader annotation push: ... created=0 updated=0 deleted=1   (the reap)

  Both requests return 200. This is not a theoretical path.

- THE EXISTING TEST IS BLIND TO IT. `tests/unit/test_920_koreader_push_only_authority.py`
  has `test_reported_delete_never_crosses_source`, whose docstring is verbatim "A KOReader
  sync must never delete a Kobo-native or web-reader highlight" -- and it passes. It only
  exercises the DIRECT delete (`annotations: []`, `deleted: [...]`). It never pushes an
  annotation carrying the existing id first, so the two-step bypass is outside its reach.
  A green test named for the invariant is exactly what kept this invisible.
- Requires an authenticated user's own KOSync credentials, so this is not a cross-user
  breach. It is a WITHIN-user integrity failure: one sync client can destroy annotations
  owned by another client of the same user, which the design explicitly promises it cannot.
- #1781 closes the adjacent hole (an UNRECOGNISED source coerced to `koreader` on create).
  This one is different: a RECOGNISED source, reassigned on update. #1781 does not fix it
  and does not claim to.

## Fix direction

Do not let a push reassign `source` on an existing row at all, or permit it only when the
new value equals the stored one. If a genuine re-home case exists, it needs an explicit
rule about who may perform it -- the current code has no rule, only a comment asserting
the outcome it wants.
title: A KOReader push can flip an existing annotation's source and then delete it, defeating the delete boundary the code claims to enforce
